title: NovusAI POC: Capacity & Autoscale scoping
summary: POC scoping focused on sizing reserved GPUs, burst strategy, and fallback policies. Discussed success criteria (latency p95, throughput, cost targets), benchmark plan, timelines, and next steps to share benchmark template and schedule a pairing session to run initial load tests.
topics: Workload sizing: qps, seq length, concurrency
Capacity model: reserved GPUs + burst nodes
Fallback strategies: lighter quantized models, regional failover
action_items: Riya Patel: Share benchmark template, test script, and model config (due 2025-08-18)
Miguel Santos: Provide current traffic traces and 7-day QPS histogram (due 2025-08-16)
Jordan Price: Share draft POC pricing for reserved + burst (due 2025-08-19)
Ava Thompson: Confirm stakeholders and internal security reviewers for Private deployment checks (due 2025-08-20)
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark repo + config
Customer to send anonymized traffic sample and current SLO targets
Schedule paired load test window (2-3 hours) next week
Follow-up call to review benchmark results and finalize POC sizing
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Riya Patel (Redwood SE), Marco Liu (Redwood), Ava Thompson (CTO, NovusAI), Miguel Santos (ML Infra), Priya Kapoor (PM)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute. Jordan from Redwood, and with me Riya and Marco.
00:14 Ava: Hi, thanks. We've got Miguel and Priya here, happy to dive in. We're mainly scoping the POC for the new chat and reranking endpoints.
00:31 Jordan: Great, goal for today is to align on success criteria, what workloads you'll run, and how we size reserved GPUs and burst strategy, and any fallback policies.
00:47 Riya: Quick intro, I tend to lead the benchmarks and infra config, Marco will help with autoscale policies.
01:05 Miguel: Quick background — prod traffic is currently about 120 qps average across two regions, peak 450 qps during spikes, median sequence len around 380 tokens for chat, embeddings workload separate. We want to test a subset for POC (chat generation + n-best rerank).
01:30 Priya: Success criteria from product side: p95 latency under 800ms for chat generation, throughput to sustain 200 qps steady, and cost per 1k tokens under our target. Also determinism isn't strict, but quality needs to match our current model baseline.
01:58 Jordan: Good, that gives us concrete numbers. A few clarifying q's: is the 450 qps peak sustained or bursts for 30-60s?
02:12 Miguel: Mostly bursts, like 20-90s, some spikes longer when batch jobs hit.
02:25 Riya: Important for autoscale — short bursts prefer burst capacity rather than scaling out reserved nodes which have longer spin-up.
02:38 Marco: We'll propose a mixed model: reserved capacity sized for baseline throughput (200 qps) plus a pool of burst instances that can be added quickly. For GPUs we usually pick reserved on a dedicated pool and burst via pre-warmed instances or a cheaper quantized variant that starts faster.
02:58 Ava: Can you explain pre-warmed vs quantized variant tradeoffs?
03:10 Marco: Sure, pre-warmed means GPU VMs already up but idle, so you pay a little but they serve immediately. Quantized variant means a smaller model (or same model with int8), lower memory and faster cold-starts, but may slightly reduce quality.
03:28 Miguel: We're sensitive to quality — benchmarks must show acceptable regression. We'll need automatic fallback policies if the quantized output drifts.
03:45 Riya: We'll include regression tests in the benchmark harness and thresholds. If measured quality (BLEU/ROUGE/top-1 rerank accuracy) drops below a set delta, we won't route to quantized variant except for cache-miss emergency.
04:05 Priya: Timeline — we'd like to start the POC next week and run 2 weeks of tests. Is that realistic?
04:17 Jordan: Yes, provided we get your traffic sample and model weights (or a reproducible prompt set). Typical POC: week 0 ingest traces/setup, week 1 run functional and small load, week 2 run extended load and finalize results.
04:35 Miguel: Security — we may need Private deployment for some data. For the POC can we run hosted with customer-managed VPC peering?
04:47 Marco: For POC we support a few options: hosted with encryption-in-transit and limited data retention, dedicated reserved nodes in our hosted VPC, or Private (VPC, or on-prem) if you require it. For quick benchmarking hosted with VPC peering or dedicated reserved is fastest.
05:10 Ava: We will check with security, but prefer to start hosted/dedicated for speed.
05:20 Jordan: Ok. On sizing — based on Miguel's baseline, we'll recommend reserved GPUs to meet 200 qps steady. For chat with median seq 380, we typically estimate tokens per second per GPU depending on model and quant. For reference, an A100-80GB can handle roughly X tokens/s for fp16, but exact numbers vary.
05:47 Riya: We'll be prescriptive after we see traces. For planning now, think in terms of concurrency: if average request is 380 tokens, and your average QPS 200, that's 76k tokens/s aggregate. At an effective 1k tokens/s per GPU (example), you'd need ~76 GPUs — obviously these numbers shift with batching and model choice. We'll run microbenchmarks to get real numbers.
06:20 Miguel: That example seems high — are there batching optimizations that reduce that?
06:28 Riya: Yes, continuous batching and prefix KV cache drastically reduce per-token cost for chat — with persistent sessions and KV caching you see effective token/s improvements. We'll test with realistic session traces.
06:40 Priya: For POC, what do you recommend for burst amortization?
06:48 Marco: Two approaches: 1) Pre-warmed burst nodes (hot standby) to cover 1.5-2x baseline for short bursts, or 2) autoscale with fast spin-up using smaller quantized instances plus a warm pool. Both have cost/latency tradeoffs — pre-warmed is lowest latency but higher idle cost. Quantized spin-up is cheaper but may add 100-600ms to p95 on cold starts.
07:12 Ava: We have a p95 SLA at 1s, so we need to ensure bursts don't push us over.
07:20 Jordan: We'll design policy: reserved capacity handles steady-state; maintain pre-warmed pool sized for typical short spike (we'll calculate target from your 90th percentile spike duration); autoscale to add additional nodes for long spikes, with cooldowns.
07:38 Miguel: What about fallback policies if capacity is saturated? We want graceful degradation, not failures.
07:46 Riya: Typical fallbacks: route to a smaller quantized model, fall back to cached responses for repeated queries, or switch regionally to a secondary region. We'll define ordered fallbacks with quality thresholds.
08:02 Priya: Is there an option to degrade response length to keep latency?
08:08 Marco: Yes you can set max generation length per policy or do partial responses, but product-wise that impacts UX. We can include adaptive length as a last-resort fallback.
08:20 Jordan: On benchmarking — we'll provide a harness with head and tail tests: functional correctness, microbenchmarks (latency, cold/warm start), and end-to-end load tests that replay traces. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
08:40 Riya: We'll include quality regression checks vs your baseline model for the same prompts. Want to confirm: you'll provide a representative set of prompts and anonymized traces?
08:51 Miguel: Yes, we'll scrub PII and share within 48 hours.
08:56 Jordan: Great. On metrics to pass the POC: list them so we can agree.
09:02 Priya: p95 latency <= 800ms for chat generation on 95% of test windows, sustain 200 qps for 1 hour continuous with acceptably low error rate (<0.1%), and cost target of <$X per 1k tokens (we'll put exact $ in follow-up). Also quality delta < 2% top-1 for rerank.
09:25 Riya: We'll parameterize those into the benchmark script so pass/fail is automatic.
09:33 Marco: Also include reliability: failover to fallback policy with no customer-visible errors for at least 95% of injected failover events.
09:43 Miguel: How do you size reserved vs burst for pricing? Do you give model/instance recommendations?
09:50 Jordan: Yes, we'll produce a POC sizing doc with recommended GPU types (e.g., A10 vs A100 vs H100) and suggested counts for reserved vs burst based on benchmark results. We'll include cost estimates for reserved commit and burst on-demand.
10:08 Priya: Any constraints on model artefacts (weights) for hosted testing? We might prefer to run our licensed weights in a Private mode.
10:18 Marco: For licensed weights we can support Private POC (bring-your-own weights) or a local VM run. Hosted test may be possible with an encrypted model blob and customer KMS, but it's slower to set up. For speed, if you can provide a smaller evaluation checkpoint or synthetic equivalent it helps.
10:40 Ava: We'll evaluate that with legal; for now we'll assume we can share a masked model or lightweight baseline for initial tests.
10:50 Jordan: Next — autoscale specifics: cooldown, scale step sizes, and warm pools. Typical defaults we propose: scale up aggressive (fast), scale down more conservative (longer cooldown) to avoid flapping. For example: scale-up threshold at 70% utilization sustained 20s, scale-up adds N nodes depending on deficit, cooldown 120s; scale-down after 5m of low utilization.
10:50 Riya: (interrupt) Also we'll set queue depth caps to keep tail latency bounded and route excess to fallback.
11:25 Miguel: What about burst billing — if pre-warmed nodes are reserved in your system do we get discount vs on-demand?
11:33 Jordan: Reserved commit for dedicated nodes is discounted; pre-warmed instances are charged at a running rate but with a different SKU sometimes. We'll send pricing scenarios in the POC pricing doc.
11:46 Priya: We also need audit logs and KMS integration verified for the POC.
11:53 Marco: We'll include sample audit logs and an architecture diagram for KMS. For Private deployments we'll surface HSM/KMS options and SAML SSO.
12:08 Riya: Ok, let's talk be more concrete on numbers. Miguel, can you confirm 7-day 95th percentile spike qps and average seq length distribution?
12:17 Miguel: I'll extract and send by Friday. 95th percentile qps about 320, median sequence length 380, 95th seq length near 740 tokens.
12:29 Jordan: Good — that longer tail sequence length will impact memory and batching, so we'll need to test long seqs in the benchmark.
12:38 Priya: For the POC, can we include a test that simulates a 5-minute surge to 400 qps?
12:44 Riya: Yes, we'll run an injected surge test and observe how autoscale behaves and whether fallbacks activate.
12:51 Jordan: We'll measure cold start times, warm recovery, and fallback latency.
13:00 Miguel: About fallback ordering — prefer cache -> quantized model -> regional failover. Is that the recommended order?
13:08 Marco: Yes generally. We'll validate with your quality checks.
13:14 Priya: Who owns rollback logic if fallback triggers too often? We want RBAC so only platform can change policies.
13:22 Jordan: We'll recommend RBAC roles: ops can adjust policies, devs can propose but can't toggle production fallback without approvals. We'll include that in the POC runbook.
13:36 Ava: For reporting, we want daily POC dashboard snapshots and a final summary report.
13:44 Riya: We'll provide dashboards with token cost breakdown, per-model latencies, and error rates — we can grant view access to your team.
13:55 Miguel: Any gotchas around K/V cache and multi-tenant memory pressure? We run multiple models in the same cluster sometimes.
14:05 Marco: We'll size KV cache per pool and recommend isolating high-volume tenants into separate pools to avoid eviction-induced latency cliffs. For POC we'll simulate mixed workloads if you want.
14:22 Priya: Let's confirm the test matrix: baseline steady state, spike test, long-tail sequence test, quality regression, failover injection.
14:33 Jordan: Yes, and we'll provide the harness with reproducible seeds for deterministic comparisons where possible.
14:44 Miguel: What about data retention and logs from POC — we need them forwarded to our Splunk.
14:52 Marco: We'll add a log-forwarding integration option; for POC we can forward to a test Splunk index.
15:02 Jordan: Ok, let's align on timeline again: you send traces and prompts by 2025-08-16, Redwood shares benchmark repo 2025-08-18, paired load test scheduled 2025-08-20 (2-3 hour window), run expanded tests 2025-08-21 to 2025-08-28, follow-up on 2025-08-29 to review results.
15:25 Priya: That works tentatively.
15:30 Ava: One more Q on metrics — can you capture per-request model variant used (fp16, int8) in metrics? We want to see exactly when fallbacks were used.
15:40 Riya: Yes, we tag requests with model variant and route id, and dashboards expose that.
15:48 Miguel: Great. On security docs — please send SOC2/ISO artifacts and our security checklist.
15:55 Jordan: We'll attach the security pack and an architecture diagram in the follow-up email.
16:05 Priya: Anything else we need to cover?
16:10 Ava: No, thanks — this was helpful.
16:15 Jordan: Quick recap — action items and next steps as discussed. We'll share the benchmark repo and POC sizing/pricing.
16:25 Miguel: Sounds good.
16:30 (call ends)
